title: Evidence in Science
text:
Scientists often rely on controlled experiments to test whether a hypothesis holds. In a well-designed study, researchers compare a treatment group with a control group that receives no intervention, so that any difference can be attributed to the variable being studied. However, a single experiment rarely provides conclusive evidence. Results usually must be replicated by independent teams before the wider scientific community accepts them.

Replication is not always straightforward, however. Some original findings fail to reproduce when other laboratories repeat the work under slightly different conditions, which has prompted a debate about publication bias. Journals tend to favour striking, positive results, so studies with null outcomes may remain unpublished. Consequently, the published literature can present a misleadingly optimistic picture of what is actually known.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what is the purpose of a control group?
options: To receive a stronger version of the treatment
To make the experiment cheaper to run
To provide a comparison so that differences can be attributed to the variable studied
To show that the hypothesis is always correct

questions.text: According to paragraph two, why might studies with null outcomes remain unpublished?
options: Because they are always poorly designed
Because journals tend to favour striking, positive results
Because other laboratories refuse to repeat them
Because they are too expensive to replicate

questions.text: What can be inferred about the published scientific literature?
options: It is a fully accurate record of all experiments conducted
It may overstate how well established some findings are
It contains only results that have been replicated
It is unaffected by the preferences of journals

questions.text: What does the passage imply about the weight of a single experiment?
options: It should be ignored entirely by researchers
It is usually sufficient to establish a scientific fact
It gains more weight once independent teams have confirmed it
It cannot involve a control group

vocabulary.definition: a proposed explanation that can be tested
repeated to produce the same result

paragraph_translations: Cientistas frequentemente dependem de experimentos controlados para testar se uma hipótese se sustenta. Em um estudo bem planejado, os pesquisadores comparam um grupo de tratamento com um grupo de controle que não recebe intervenção, de modo que qualquer diferença possa ser atribuída à variável estudada. No entanto, um único experimento raramente fornece evidências conclusivas. Os resultados normalmente precisam ser replicados por equipes independentes antes que a comunidade científica mais ampla os aceite.

A replicação, porém, nem sempre é simples. Alguns achados originais não se reproduzem quando outros laboratórios repetem o trabalho em condições um pouco diferentes, o que tem provocado um debate sobre viés de publicação. Os periódicos tendem a favorecer resultados marcantes e positivos, de modo que estudos com resultados nulos podem permanecer não publicados. Consequentemente, a literatura publicada pode apresentar um quadro enganosamente otimista do que realmente se sabe.
